incidents.name: Login errors for subset of Slack Enterprise Grid customers

incident_updates.body: This incident has been resolved. Login via Slack is operating normally again, and no further action is required.

Some customers on Slack Enterprise Grid who sign in with Slack are seeing Slack-originating errors when logging in. 

We've raised this with Slack and are monitoring for a fix. 

Customers using SAML sign-in aren't affected.

Alert ingestion and our On-call product's paging functionality are unaffected.

Latency has now returned to normal.

Between 13:00 and 15:08 UTC there were periods of increased latency from some Microsoft APIs. Messages in Microsoft Teams were delivered with increased latency. Our dashboard and mobile app were not affected.
We are continuing to see periods of increased latency with our Microsoft Teams app. All other surfaces, including the dashboard and our mobile app, remain unaffected.
We have identified increased latency in our Microsoft Teams app. We are currently investigating how this is impacting our platform and we will update with more information shortly as we learn more.

We observed a limited increase in latency as well as a small number of dashboard errors between 19:31:30 and 19:34:30 UTC. This affected 0\.03% of calls to our dashboard. This was detected by our internal synthetic monitoring. 

The cause of these elevated errors was due to networking issues within GCP at the time. This is confirmed by our logs showing our GCP load balancer not forwarding success responses, as well as network timeouts when trying to reach external services. 

The impact was limited to a small number of users and was solved by refreshing the dashboard.

incidents.name: Increased rate of disconnections from Sentry

incident_updates.body:
We have managed to re-establish a connection to Sentry for almost all of the affected customers. If Sentry is still showing up as disconnected, you will need to remove the incident.io integration from the Sentry side, and then go through the reinstallation flow by opening incident.io and going to Settings → Integrations → Sentry.

If you do this, please note that Sentry will remove the "Notify incident.io" action from alert rules when you uninstall the integration. If that was the only action in the alert rule, the entire rule is disabled. You will therefore need to verify any alert rules after re-installing.

We have confirmed that we are able to restore these connections, and we are now in the process of restoring these. When this happens, you'll see that the Sentry integration no longer flags up as requiring reconnection. Once we have finished restoring access, we'll post another update here.
We've verified a fix locally, and we're starting to roll this out in production now.
We're currently testing the fix that will allow us to re-connect any disconnected Sentry integrations on behalf of customers, and will have another update on this in 30 minutes.

Please don't uninstall our application from Sentry: we are working to restore these connections on our side, and no action is currently required. We will provide an update in 30 minutes.

Between 12:46 and 12:50 UTC, some requests to our web dashboard and API failed. Some interactions via Slack, Teams and the mobile app were also affected by this.

Critical areas of our application were **unaffected**, including on-call alert notifications, alert ingestion flows, status pages, and background event processing.

The root cause of the failure was in the routing of traffic to application servers, within our internal load balancing infrastructure.

We're working to enhance our resilience to this issue in the future.
